Cathode import premiums have declined again over the past two weeks, and according to market insiders are now around the $60/t mark. With the Q2 seasonal pick up in demand not having materialised, sentiment is bearish putting downward pressure on prices and premiums. The negative SHFE /LME arbitrage has also widened again as LME prices have moved up ahead of SHFE prices. EW premiums have also declined slightly, particularly at the top of the price range and are now in the US$50-60/t range. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **July 2012** www.crugroup.com After rising in early June, stocks in Shanghai bonded warehouses declined a little during the second half of June, down to 500,000t, with a further 50,000t in Guangdong. Market sources suggest that the level of cathode exports fell sharply from early June, and this is supported by the LME Asian warehouse stocks data. As described in previous issues, much of the export activity during May and early June was attributed to Chinese smelters covering short positions on the LME, and the material was shipped to Asian warehouses. With a decline in cathode exports offsetting the combined impact of the continued negative arbitrage and weak underlying fundamentals on imports, we expect that the June import data will show little change from the May levels. Looking ahead, Chinese companies are cutting the use of copper as collateral for loans, which will weigh on future imports. Tight credit and high interest rates prompted borrowers to raise loans against physical metal, but the key discount rate used for short term loans has now fallen back below 5%. # Market fundamentals remain weak The expected Q2 seasonal pick up in demand failed to materialise, and market insiders report that sentiment amongst semi fabricators is bearish. Most are pessimistic about the outlook in the near term and capacity utilisation rates remain poor, with the result that cathode inventories are being kept to minimum levels and fabricators are being cautious in their purchasing strategy. However inventories remain high throughout the supply chain. In addition to the overhang of refined copper inventories, some sectors still have high product inventories; air conditioner manuf

acturers, for example, have high inventories of air conditioning units and copper tube, with a negative impact on their demand for tube. However things may not be as bad as they seem. The situation for the semi fabricators is being exacerbated by a rise in capacity, meaning a reduction in market share for each producer. This is particularly true for flat rolled products. Also negative for demand is the announcement that the Guangzhou municipal government will limit the sale of cars for 12 months from July 1st 2012. Sales will be limited to 120,000 over the course of the year, resulting in a reduction of around 50% in total sales in the city. Guangzhou is the fourth city after Shanghai, Beijing and Guiyang to limit vehicle sales. On the supply side of the equation, refined copper production continues to rise, supported by increased imports of concentrates and scrap and rising domestic mine output. Although growth slowed in April and May, according to official data, total cathode output was up by 10.7% y-o-y during January to May, while domestic mine output rose by 17% y-o-y in the first four months of the year. Chinese smelters have benefited from the closure of the PASAR smelter and refinery in the Philippines, which has resulted in some additional concentrates becoming available for Chinese smelters. New refinery capacity continues to be added; June output is being boosted by the start up of an additional 100,000t/y refining capacity at Shandong Fangyuan’s operation, Shandong Jinsheng has completed its expansion of secondary capacity from 100,000t/y to 200,000t/y, and Shenyang Xingye has successfully produced the first batch of refined copper from its 50,000t/y of new refinery capacity. Yunnan Tin’s new smelter and refinery experienced technological problems on start up, however, and is currently closed, but a restart is expected soon. However, in Sichuan province, the local government of Shifang has ordered the cancellation of Sichuan Hongda Molybdenum and Copper’s new 400,000t/y smelter and refinery project, citing environmental reasons. The order follows protests by local residents over the environmental impact of the plant, which also included a © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **July 2012** www.crugroup.com 40,000t/y molybdenum facility. The project, which was to use flash smelting and converting technology and included an acid plant, had been approved by the Ministry of Environmental Protection in March. This is the first example in China of a new and technically advanced project being cancelled due to pressure from local groups. With environmental awareness increasing in China it may not be the last, and this will have significant implications for the rate of growth of the smelting and refining industry in China. # SHFE copper prices pulled up by LME SHFE 3-month price SHFE inventory on the up again

The LME copper price has continued to be volatile over the last two weeks, reacting to economic and political events in Europe. After a rally in mid-June, the price turned down again as the financial difficulties in Spain and Italy prompted investors to flee to safe haven investments. However, it rallied again in the wake of the Eurozone summit, where the decision was taken to allow the European Stability Mechanism to recapitalise banks, and investors moved back into more risky assets. The 3-month price hit a trading high of 7,819/t on 3rd July. The cash-to-3 month spread has remained in a small contango. The SHFE is currently trading at around RMB55,000-56,000/t. It has risen more modestly than the LME price over the last two weeks, and the negative arbitrage has widened again to over $100/t. In China, the relationship between the physical market price and the SHFE cash month price has fluctuated between backwardation and contango, most recently being in contango, while although the backwardation between the SHFE cash-month and 3-month prices persists, it has narrowed to just $200-300/t over the last week. These price movements reflect the surplus availability of cathode in the Chinese market which has also resulted in a rise in SHFE stocks. The cathode inventory in SHFE warehouses totalled 155,237t on July 6th , up by 15,800t on the previous week. With final demand remaining weak and the stock overhang persisting, it seems likely that prices will come under downward pressure and will be unable to respond to any upward movement in the LME, resulting in a widening of the negative arbitrage. We expect that the SHFE price will continue to trade in the RMB52,00057,000 range over the next two weeks. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 4 **July 2012** www.crugroup.com ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Wan Ling (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2183 ling.wan@crugroup.com **Christine Meilton (London):** +44 20 7903 2098 christine.meilton@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 22nd June 2012.
